message.content:
I’m not able to create or register a real SQL Server instance myself—those actions require administrative access to your infrastructure. However, I can walk you through the typical process of provisioning a new Microsoft SQL Server (or Azure‑SQL) so you can point it at `http://plgah.ca` once it’s ready. --- ### Quick checklist – “Add a New SQL Server” | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **1️⃣ Choose hosting** | • On‑premises VM / physical machine
• Cloud provider (Azure VMs, AWS RDS, GCP Cloud SQL)
• Managed service (Azure SQL Database, Amazon Aurora, etc.) | Pick based on cost, scalability, maintenance level. | | **2️⃣ Provision resources** | • Allocate CPU/RAM/disk.
• Set OS version compatible with desired SQL Server edition. | Ensures performance meets workload needs. | | **3️⃣ Install/Deploy SQL Server** | • For self‑hosted: run installer (`sqlservr.exe`).
• For managed services: use portal/API to spin up database. | Installs engine & configures basic settings. | | **4️⃣ Network exposure** | • Expose port 1433 over HTTPS/TLS if using remote connections.
• Configure firewall rules/IP whitelisting.
• If behind reverse proxy, map `/sqlserver` path to TCP 1433. | Allows clients to reach the DB securely. | | **5️⃣ Create logical databases** | • Use SSMS or T-SQL scripts to create required schemas/tables. | Organizes data per business domain. | | **6️⃣ Security hardening** | • Enable Transparent Data Encryption (TDE).
• Enforce strong passwords, MFA for admin accounts.
• Apply least‑privilege roles. | Protects sensitive information. | | **7️⃣ Backup strategy** | • Full backups nightly + differential hourly.
• Store offsite snapshots. | Enables recovery after failure. | | **8️⃣ Monitoring & alerts** | • Setup health checks (CPU, memory, disk usage).
• Alert on connection failures or slow queries. | Keeps uptime high and issues visible early. | --- #### Example: Deploying a Basic Windows VM + SQL Server on Azure ```bash az vm create \ --resource-group myRG \ --name sqlVM01 \ --image Win2019Datacenter \ --admin-user azureUser \ --generate-ssh-keys # Connect to VM az ssh vm -g myRG -n sqlVM01 # Inside VM: powershell -Command " $installerPath = '\\path\to\MSSQLInstaller.msi' Start-MSIInstall -SourceFile $installerPath ` /qn INSTALLLEVEL=100 ISACCEPTEDEULA=TRUE " ``` After installation: * Open Remote Desktop → Port 3389 * In SQL Server Configuration Manager → enable TCP/IP, set IP addresses, restart MSSQLSERVER service. * Add inbound rule in NSG allowing traffic from your client subnet to port 1433. Once everything is running, you’ll see the public DNS name of the VM (e.g., `sqlvm01.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com`) – this becomes your *endpoint*. You can then expose it under `http://plgah.ca/sqlserver` via a reverse proxy such as Nginx or IIS URL Rewrite module. --- ### Need More Help? If you’re looking for step‑by‑step commands tailored to a particular cloud platform or want to automate deployment with Terraform/Azure ARM templates, let me know! Also, clarify whether you intend to host the SQL Server yourself or just need to connect to an existing one at that address.
